anomalies.observed: In the 'Capacitive Touch Button (TSC)' block on the root sheet, the 22 nF capacitor C2 (to GND), the 1 k series resistor R5 (whose other end drives the electrode A3 pin BTN), and BOTH net labels NET0004 (MCU PB5, pin 37) and NET0007 (MCU PB7, pin 39) are all joined at one node. This merges the two Touch-Sensing-Controller group pins and places the sampling capacitor on the same net as the electrode drive.
anomalies.expected: The specification requires two separate nets: TSC_G2_IO2 = PB5 -> series resistor -> electrode, and TSC_G2_IO4 = PB7 -> 22 nF sampling capacitor -> GND. The sampling capacitor must sit only on the dedicated Cx pin (PB7), isolated from the electrode/series-resistor net.

evidence.quote: Page 1, 'Capacitive Touch Button (TSC)': C2 22n to GND, NET0004 and NET0007 stacked on the left terminal of R5 1k, R5 right terminal to A3 BTN (TSC)
TSC_G2_IO2: U2 pin 57 (PB5) — R8 (1 kΩ series resistor) — A2 pin "BTN" ... TSC_G2_IO4: U2 pin 59 (PB7) — C14 (22 nF to GND) — this is the TSC sampling capacitor for the group

anomalies.impact: The STM32 TSC charge-transfer measurement relies on the sampling capacitor being on a pin separate from the driven electrode; tying PB5 and PB7 together and hanging the sampling cap on the electrode net defeats the touch sensing (and shorts two MCU GPIOs), so the capacitive touch button will not operate as intended.
